title: Diljit Dosanjh Dropped the Main Vaapas Aaunga Trailer Mid-Concert in Toronto. North America Gets Tickets Before India.
excerpt: Imtiaz Ali's love story pairs Diljit with Sharvari, Vedang Raina, and Naseeruddin Shah. Advance bookings open in the US and Canada a full week before Indian ticket sales begin on June 12.
body:
The trailer did not premiere on YouTube. It did not premiere at a press event in Mumbai. It premiered on the stadium screens of a packed concert venue in Toronto, while Diljit Dosanjh was mid-set on his AURA Tour 2026.

Thousands of fans — mostly Indian-origin, mostly singing along to every word of his Punjabi hits — watched the first extended look at *Main Vaapas Aaunga*, Imtiaz Ali's new film, projected above the stage. The reaction, captured in dozens of fan-shot clips that immediately flooded social media, was not the polite applause of a film industry event. It was the roar of a diaspora audience that recognised what they were seeing: a major Bollywood film being unveiled for them first, in their city, on their terms.

## The Film

*Main Vaapas Aaunga* is Imtiaz Ali's return to the director's chair after *Chamkila*, his 2024 collaboration with Diljit that earned widespread acclaim. The new film stars Diljit Dosanjh alongside Vedang Raina, Sharvari Wagh, and the great Naseeruddin Shah. A.R. Rahman has composed the score, with lyrics by Irshad Kamil — the same partnership that produced the music for *Rockstar*, *Tamasha*, and *Highway*.

The story, in keeping with Ali's signature territory, explores love, longing, and the passage of time. The trailer suggests a narrative that moves between present and past, with Diljit and Naseeruddin Shah's characters appearing to be connected across different timelines. Vedang Raina and Sharvari appear to carry the younger timeline, with a chemistry that the trailer leans into heavily.

## The Diaspora-First Strategy

Here is the detail that matters most: advance bookings for *Main Vaapas Aaunga* will open in the United States and Canada a full week before they open in India. The film releases theatrically on June 12, but North American audiences will be able to secure seats before anyone in Mumbai or Delhi can.

This is not an accident. It is a deliberate strategy that reflects a reality the Indian film industry has been slow to acknowledge. Diljit Dosanjh's concert tours regularly sell out arenas across North America. His AURA Tour plays to audiences who buy tickets at Western concert prices, who consume Punjabi and Hindi content on streaming platforms, and who show up for films in numbers that have made North America a top-three territory for major Indian releases.

The Toronto trailer premiere was both marketing and message: the diaspora is not the afterthought market. It is the first market.

## The Music

The soundtrack has already begun rolling out. The latest release, *Ishq Mastana*, dropped on Vedang Raina's birthday and features a central refrain drawn from Sant Kabir's timeless verses — "Haman Hai Ishq Mastana, Haman Ko Hoshiyari Kya." Sung by Mohit Chauhan alongside Nargis and Pooja Tiwari, composed by Rahman, and written by Kamil, the track blends classical devotional poetry with a contemporary Bollywood sensibility. An earlier track, *Maskara*, has already gone viral on social media.

## What to Watch For

Imtiaz Ali's films live or die on two things: the emotional authenticity of the central relationship and the music. With Rahman behind the score and a cast that pairs the raw star power of Diljit with the classical gravitas of Naseeruddin Shah and the emerging appeal of Vedang Raina and Sharvari, the ingredients are assembled. Whether the story delivers is a question only June 12 can answer.

The film is produced by Birla Studios and Applause Entertainment, with Window Seat Films. Music is on Tips.
